description: F129 (Sprint 51): Review No Rule Items screen -- account filter and the covered-item sweep's reload path. COVERS the Sprint 50 surfaces MT-3 (the screen is reachable -- post-F135 it IS the home screen when accounts exist, so reachability is proven by its account-filter face resolving on launch, not by an entry-point click) and MT-2c (sweep runs on every load). READ-ONLY: drives the account-filter dropdown and navigates only -- creates no rules, adds no safe senders, marks nothing processed -- so it is inherently net-zero on the dev DB; every filter change is restored to All Accounts before the script ends. TWO HARNESS CONSTRAINTS drove this design (Sprint 51 discovery, both re-confirmed live): (1) `ww_assert*` is NOT replayable by the script runner (README line 195) -- a case containing only asserts reports FAILED even when the UI is correct, so verification here is expressed as CLICKS: a click that resolves proves the element exists with that exact name, and a missing element errors the step. (2) The Windows UIA projection of Flutter semantics surfaces only widgets carrying a `tooltip:` plus screen titles and Text nodes; `Semantics(label:)` on a merged container does NOT project, so account ROWS are unaddressable by name and are deliberately not used. SELECTORS VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-28 against dev build 0.5.8; REWORKED 2026-08-15 (Sprint 59) for F135/F155; REPAIRED 2026-08-23 (Sprint 62 sweep) for F169 (Sprint 61): the horizontally-scrolling account filter CHIPS were replaced by a single-select DROPDOWN (PopupMenuButton faced by a Chip). The face projects as a Text node named with the ACTIVE selection and its live count (e.g. 'All Accounts (3)'); the open menu's entries project as Buttons with the same 'label (count)' names. THE FACE DOES NOT RESPOND TO InvokePattern -- ww_invoke/ww_click-with-invoke reports success WITHOUT opening the menu (verified live 2026-08-23) -- so every face click uses ww_click with useInvokePattern:false (physical mouse). Face = Text, menu entry = Button, so the two are never ambiguous even when the open menu contains the same label as the face. Every face click OPENS the menu, so each is paired with a menu-entry selection that closes it; a bare existence-proof of the face is expressed as the pair (open, re-select).

testCases.title: Post-F135 home screen renders the F169 account-filter dropdown; reload re-runs the sweep; navigation round-trip survives

steps._comment: PRIMING QUERY -- also guarantees a maximized window so nothing is off-screen.

MT-3 (post-F135 form): the app opens ON the Review No Rule Items screen when accounts exist. The account-filter FACE exists only on this screen, so it resolving IS the reachability proof. MT-2c evidence: the face carries the post-sweep total in its name -- counts are data-dependent, prefix match keeps the script valid across scans. This click OPENS the dropdown menu.
Menu entry resolving proves the menu actually opened (F169 contract); clicking it selects the AOL account and closes the menu.

SETTLE BUFFER: the runner replays no ww_wait (re-confirmed 2026-08-23 -- it SKIPS the step), and a face click dispatched during the popup-close animation is swallowed by the closing barrier (observed twice live: the next menu query then times out). A harmless resolving click on the static screen title costs one selector round-trip, which outlasts the close animation. Same class of harmless-click-as-anchor as f124's label clicks.
PROOF OF EFFECT: the face is RENAMED to the active selection -- it resolving under the AOL name proves the filter genuinely applied. Opens the menu again.
